G2 = current + previous pregnancy.
P1 = twins count as one parity (para counts deliveries ≥20 wk, not babies)

ACE inhibitors are teratogenic (fetal renal dysgenesis, oligohydramnios, skull defects) → stop before conception.
Safe: methyldopa, labetalol, nifedipine

Lactational amenorrhoea: suckling ↑es prolactin → ↓es GnRH → anovulation.
β-hCG is negative (not pregnant) & TSH is normal

Didelphys → transverse lie/malpresentation, preterm labour, recurrent abortion.
Endometriosis is not a typical feature of the anomaly itself
Septate uterus: hysteroscopic septum resection (no uterine incision), indicated in recurrent pregnancy loss
HSG: radio-opaque dye fills the uterine cavity & both tubes (spill = patency); done in the proliferative phase
Unruptured ectopic, β-hCG <5000, no rupture/haemodynamic instability → single-dose methotrexate (50 mg/m²)
Cornual fibroids obstructing the tubal ostia → myomectomy is the corrective option when ovulation & semen analysis are normal

OCP suppresses ovulation → LMP unreliable.
CRL in the 1st trimester is the most accurate dating parameter
Stepwise devascularisation in PPH: uterine → ovarian → internal iliac artery ligation

Cannonball lung mets = metastatic GTN → multi-agent EMA-CO.
Single-agent methotrexate is for low-risk disease
Active genital herpes at labour → acyclovir + elective LSCS to prevent neonatal herpes

OP position: back is posterior, limbs anterior → infraumbilical flattening.
FHS is heard laterally (in the flank)

Superfecundation = 2 ova of the same cycle fertilised by sperm from separate coital acts (can be different fathers).
Superfoetation = conceptions in different cycles
Obstructive anomaly → retrograde menstruation → endometriosis (cyclical/chronic pelvic pain)
Mid-cycle ↑ estrogen → profuse, clear, non-itchy cervical mucus = physiological discharge (around ovulation)
APLA: recurrent fetal loss + early-onset preeclampsia (placental vessel thrombosis) → aspirin + LMWH
Missed active OCPs early in the pack → continue the current pack c̅ additional (barrier) contraception for the next days
Warfarin crosses the placenta (embryopathy, fetal/neonatal bleeding) → shift to LMW heparin near term
Indomethacin ↓es prostaglandins → premature closure of the ductus arteriosus (late pregnancy)
Prolapse + leak on cough = ↑ intra-abdominal pressure overcoming weak urethral support → stress incontinence

Umbilical arteries (2): deoxygenated blood fetus → placenta.
Umbilical vein (1): oxygenated blood placenta → fetus
Mid-cycle ↑ estrogen → profuse, clear, non-itchy cervical mucus = physiological discharge (around ovulation)
Declining FHR + dilatation crossing the action line despite oxytocin → fetal distress/labour arrest → LSCS
Polyhydramnios: SFH > gestational age (41 cm at 36 wk), tense abdomen, fetal parts not palpable, muffled FHS

Asherman (intrauterine adhesions): hysteroscopic adhesiolysis is diagnostic + therapeutic.
Subserosal fibroid lies outside the cavity
Iron supplementation starts after the 1st trimester (~14 wk): nausea settles & demand ↑es in 2nd-3rd trimester
Infertility = no conception after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse; only 6 months → reassure & review

Lateral parametrial involvement = FIGO IIB → chemoradiation (cisplatin + EBRT + brachytherapy).
Surgery is for early-stage disease
Genital TB: chronic low-grade pelvic pain, scanty discharge, menstrual irregularity/intermenstrual bleeding

Laparoscopic energy devices can cause unrecognised thermal injury (bowel/ureter) with delayed presentation.
Advantages: ↓es pain, ↓es bleeding, faster recovery
Transverse lie at 36-37 wk, adequate liquor, normal placenta, multipara → ECV can be attempted
Unruptured ectopic, stable, hCG <5000, mass <3.5 cm → single-dose IM methotrexate
HMG induction + abdominal pain, vomiting, breathlessness + enlarged multicystic ovary → OHSS (↑ VEGF → ↑ vascular permeability → third-spacing)
Absorption of distension fluid → volume overload → pulmonary oedema (immediate); dilutional hyponatraemia c̅ hypotonic fluids
Tender red swelling at the lower labia = Bartholin duct blockage + infection → Bartholin abscess
Cervical cancer is HPV-driven (16/18), not hereditary → HPV vaccine for the daughter
CAIS (46,XY): androgen receptor defect → normal breasts (peripheral aromatisation), scanty pubic/axillary hair, blind vagina, absent uterus, inguinal testes
Primary amenorrhoea c̅ cyclical pain & bulging introital mass → haematocolpos from imperforate hymen

G2 = current + previous pregnancy.
P1 = twin delivery counts as one parity
Supine hypotension syndrome: gravid uterus compresses the IVC → ↓es venous return; relieved by left lateral position
Luteal phase: corpus luteum ↑es progesterone (peak ~day 21-22) → negative feedback ↓es LH & FSH
Controlled cord traction (Brandt-Andrews): suprapubic counter-pressure c̅ steady cord traction, part of AMTSL
Cord prolapse: relieve cord compression (elevate presenting part, retrograde bladder filling) → emergency LSCS as cervix is not fully dilated
AUB c̅ thickened endometrium at ≥45 yr → endometrial biopsy to exclude hyperplasia/carcinoma

Pritchard: 4 g IV + 10 g IM (5 g each buttock) = 14 g loading.
Maintenance: 5 g IM 4-hourly, alternate buttocks
Atonic PPH unresponsive to uterotonics → uterine balloon tamponade (Bakri) before surgical options
Postmenopausal painless bleeding = endometrial carcinoma until proved otherwise
VBAC c̅ fetal bradycardia + maternal tachycardia = suspected scar rupture → immediate emergency LSCS
Shoulder dystocia: McRoberts → Rubin → Gaskin → Zavanelli (Zavanelli = last resort)
Episiotomy repair: vaginal mucosa → perineal muscle → skin
Adenomyosis: MRI shows thickened/blurred junctional zone (>12 mm) c̅ globular uterus
Postmenopausal bleeding needs work-up first: pelvic exam, Pap smear & TVS (± endometrial biopsy); hypertension doesn't explain it
Age <40 c̅ amenorrhoea, FSH >25 IU/L & very low AMH = premature ovarian insufficiency

1st-trimester dating: CRL is the most accurate (±5-7 days).
BPD/AC are used later
↑ Prolactin ↓es GnRH pulsatility → ↓es LH/FSH → anovulation, amenorrhoea & infertility
Hydronephrosis/non-functioning kidney due to tumour = FIGO IIIB

Løvset: 180° rotation of the trunk, delivering the arms/shoulders one by one.
Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit is for the after-coming head

Chadwick's sign (bluish cervix) is a probable sign of pregnancy.
Confirmed pregnancy needs fetal heart/parts/USG
High-risk caesarean (BMI >35 + preeclampsia) → LMWH thromboprophylaxis

Normal cord: 2 arteries + 1 vein (in Wharton's jelly).
Single umbilical artery → associated anomalies
Past toxoplasmosis c̅ IgG +ve = immunity; fetal risk is mainly from primary infection during pregnancy
Amniotic band syndrome: fibrous bands entangle fetal parts → limb/digit amputation, constriction rings
Cardinal (Mackenrodt) ligament = main uterine support; weakness → uterine prolapse (multiparity, unskilled delivery)
Serous cystadenocarcinoma: commonest epithelial ovarian cancer, CA-125 ↑es, often bilateral, psammoma bodies
